subjects.candidate_subject: Retain the stored continuation throughout a stack walk
subjects.baseline_subject: [GR-81123] Preserve pending initialization writes across control-flow merges
subjects.head: 6f55b27d87897825f2a53af3b0a5bdbd7650aef8

independence: Reviewed exact diff and source invariants (walker, pointer rebasing, resume, allocation publication) before reading prior continuation logs and continuation-second.json. No source modifications, mx builds/style, subagents, remote CI, paid services, or arbitrary direct Continuation.run experiments.
reasoning: updateStackPointerForContinuation translates cached start/end/current SP using the address delta of the stored object. A replacement StoredContinuation is a different stack layout; capturing once per initialized continuation restores the invariant.

The retained stored reference roots the original object. Resuming copies its frames to the carrier; it does not destroy the stored frame bytes. GC updates object references; raw pointers are rebased inside uninterruptible sections before physical access. Interpreter capture also rebases against the retained object.

Physical advancement may query metadata interruptibly, but the next pointer dereference is preceded by rebasing. AOT image code is explicitly guaranteed on this path; omitted fork runtime-code tethers do not weaken this upstream AOT invariant.

When the current continuation is exhausted, stored=null and initialized=false precede parent traversal and initialization. Scope matching does not change within an initialized continuation. No promise of atomic snapshot across a mutable parent hierarchy is added.
Completion after capture leaves the stored reference reachable and the old frames readable through final traversal. invalidate clears continuation and stored at end or when the stream callback exits.

Capture occurs at first physical advancement. A concurrent resume before capture may expose null/new state; this existing initialization boundary is neither solved nor made worse. allocateToYield fills before publishing stored, and initializeForContinuation treats a null IP as unwalkable.

The committed regression uses normal virtual-thread park/unpark. JDK threadState maps PARKING to RUNNABLE and PARKED to WAITING, supporting the phase/state handshake here. The test demonstrates internal Native Image behavior; it is not a portable public concurrent StackWalker guarantee.

nonblocking_observations.observation: Cleanup follows the walk instead of using finally. A failure can leave the daemon virtual thread parked and its captured state retained until test-image exit. Consider finally-based release/join for test isolation; not a production correctness blocker.

experiments.name: native probe build
experiments.result: Built in 15.1 seconds; reported peak RSS 1.32 GiB. Two experimental-option warnings for reflection config.

experiments.name: interleaved virtual-thread walks
experiments.result: 8 cases / 16 walks; exact original frame-list equality. Two repetitions each of unchanged snapshot, larger replacement, larger then shallower replacement, and completion. Transition after half the frames. Each case has two active walkers and fresh replacement-stack observation. Allocation and System.gc between every frame pair.

experiments.name: GC and assertions verification
experiments.result: Same 8 cases / 16 walks pass; 160 full GC events recorded. This confirms collections, not precise relocation counts or assertion compilation coverage.
